In the Surrey Youths held at Tooting on May 27th we had a fair measure of success, and Frank Kemp won the 100 yards in the good time of 10.9 secs.
We managed to win both these matches and Frank Kemp scored a fine double when winning the Junior 100 and 220 yards. Ray Tooby was runner-up in the 880 Junior event and D.
On the same evening a Junior match was held, and in this we fared a little better, and once again Frank Kemp scored a double win in the 100 and 220 yards.
In the Junior match, Frank Kemp scored a good double by winning the 100 and 220, and Bob Wolton was second in the 440, while Maclean won the 880 yards and Ray Tooby the mile.

Basil Walden won the senior 100 yards and Frank Kemp followed suit in the junior event at this distance. Odde was second in the quarter and Gerry Trower won the junior 880 in good style and Ches Walker was also first home in the senior half-mile.

In the 100 yards (under 19) we only had five runners and Frank Kemp was the winner in the good time of 10.4 seconds. We made up two heats in the 100 yards Boys (under 16) race and the final was won by Don Clements from Malden.
Frank Kemp won the 100 yards in 10.5 and the 220 in 23.3 which is good running for a Junior and Frank seems destined for the highest honours when he competes as a Senior.

This was won by Alan Law, who just beat John Briggs, with Frank Kemp a close third. The 3 miles walk saw the field start off their time allowances and Joe Wilson, who went off the limit mark, set a good strong pace and was never headed.

Archie Bedford ran a good race to beat Pudicombe of S.L.H. in the 2 miles, with Eric Herbert in third place, and the final points position was :—Belgrave H., 33; South London H., 16; Leicester, 5. In the junior match we had Ian Forrester winning the 100, with Frank Kemp taking the 220 and P.
Frank Kemp won the junior 100 and was second in the furlong, and Peter Hunt finished second in the quarter, with Gerry Trower in a similar position in the half-mile.

This match was held in conjunction with the " Gordon Stewart " Trophy contest at Drayton Green, and our juniors once again came out on top. Frank Kemp won the 100 yards, with Alan Law taking the 220, and Doug Maclean won the half-mile, with J.
Casselton give us the lead, which was held by both Frank Kemp and Alan Law, but Gerry Trower could not match the strong finish of Hewson of Mitcham, and so we finished second in this event.

We were pleased to see Doug Whitehead turning out for us in the javelin throw and he gained second place with 147 ft. 2 ins. In the junior events, Frank Kemp was beaten by an old rival in Breacker of Mitcham, and Ken Eales was second in the 220 yards.

In the junior match, Ian Forrester won the 100 yards, with Ken Eales third, and Frank Kemp won the 220, as usual, we might say. Gerry Trower was beaten by Boyd of Wallington in a close finish for the 880 yards in the good time of 2 mins. 2.4 secs., and Geoff Goode won the 1 mile in 4 mins. 41.6 secs.
Bergvalds was second in the weight and third in the discus throw. Frank Kemp was second in the Junior 100 yards, but won the 220 in 22.8 seconds, which is some going for a junior.

Godfrey won the 880 yards and Frank Kemp obliged, as usual, in the 220, with Geoff Goode taking the mile. We also won the sprint relay, and final points for the junior match were:—Belgrave, 19; Mitcham, 13; S.L.H., 4.

After a very close struggle we managed to beat Whitgift by a single point, with the Ruskin and John Fisher boys well behind. Frank Kemp scored a double win in the 100 and 220 yards, and Ian Forrester won the second string race in the latter event.
Junior handicap we only had one heat, and the winner was J. Thomas, who is quite a promising recruit to our sprinting ranks, with Frank Kemp second and Ian Forrester third.
Thomas and Ian Forrester were runners-up to Breacker, of Mitcham, in the 100 yards, and Frank Kemp was second in the 220 and appeared unable to negotiate the rather sharp bends at this track.

Maclean jumped for us in the High Jump and Gordon Lowers turned out in the Long Jump and Javelin events. We fared much better in the junior match, with Frank Kemp having a dual sprint victory, as did P.
The holder, Denis Merrett, was unable to run owing to injury. Frank Kemp retained his 100 yards junior title with P.
Frank Kemp won the 100 yards, with Ian Forrester third, and Frank was also second in the 220 yards. Don Maclean was second in the 880 and Geoff Goode occupied a similar position in the 1 mile.
Cornish second and Frank Kemp third. The latter ran well off a back mark but is considering taking it easy for the next season or two.

The Shot Putt handicap was won by Les Stokell who is now taking up field events, he has ideas about becoming a decathion performer, and he certainly did well to take first place in the handicap with Frank Kemp second and a new member in R.
Many of our promising Junior members are now doing their National Service, and we have recently seen Frank Kemp join the R.A.F. and Peter Courtney and R.

We scored a good win in the 1 mile medley relay and final points were: Herne Hill H., 59; Belgrave H., 38; Woodford Green A.C., 25. In the Junior events we had Benstead and Forrester in the first two places in the 100 yards, while Frank Kemp won the 220.

There was also a Junior match between the same clubs and in this we had Frank Kemp winning the 100 with John Benstead taking the 220 yards, while Geoff Goode was second to a very promising local youngster in the 1 mile.

In the Junior events we had Frank Kemp 2nd in the 220 yards, with Geoff Goode also 2nd in the 1 mile. The Kent championships saw Ray Tooby win the Senior 1 mile with Jack Brown in second place and the time was 4 min. 19.6 secs.

Gregory won the 2 miles walk in 14 min. 12.4 secs., and this was our only other success except that our Junior team of Frank Kemp, Alan Law, Ian Forrester and John Benstead won the 4 x 110 yards Junior relay, beating Poly H. and the R.A.F., Halton, in 45.2 secs.
The 100 yards junior final resulted in a win for Alan Law with Frank Kemp second and J.

He finished 2nd, running for Ford Motors S.C. Frank Kemp also recorded a time of 10.02 secs. in the P.O. Championships, 1951, but this was on a little known grass track.
Maddicks, our young javelin thrower, who, with 14ft. 6in., did 43ft. 3¾in. Frank Kemp (11ft.) was second, with Ian Forrester (16ft. 6in.) third, and the scratch man, Gaworski, did 41ft. 3¼in.

Frank Kemp is now out in the Middle East with the R.A.F., and sends best wishes to all his Club-mates. He has a brother of Basil Walden stationed with him and says he has done 10.1 for the 100 and 22.5 for the 220, so keep up the good work, Frank !
The 440 was a triumph for Frank Kemp who won in a personal best of 51.9. The 880 was won by Poly's Australian International Douglas in 2.08 with George Davidson returning 2.1.8.

The 440 yards proved to be a race of successes for Belgrave in that Brian Morris won in the time of 50.9s. with Frank Kemp 3rd in 52. We also had a victory in the 100 yards in which Ivan Mayers and Denis Merrett finished 1st and 2nd.

It is with regret that the Club have accepted the resignation of FRANK KEMP. Frank will be remembered for his excellent sprinting as a Junior in the early "fifties".
